## 18. Target-action framing and a second fresh comparison

The V3 policy passed its exposed development cases but failed the frozen criterion on fresh controlled cases.
It returned seven of eight required fresh additions, with no clear extras. All three fresh cases required native fallback.
The proposed verdict is to keep this recipe experimental. This result supports neither automatic adoption nor a whole-task savings claim.

### Question, freeze, and budget

The question was whether explicit target-action framing improved selection with the reviewed CLI requirement protected.
V3 removed evaluator restrictions from two target tasks. It also protected craft-cli in the gate-wrapper case, following the reviewer's confirmed requirement.
The candidate descriptions, questions, criteria, and 0.20/0.80 uncertainty band stayed unchanged.
The protected CLI requirement is deterministic preservation, not recovered model accuracy.

The first stage reused six now-exposed V2 cases. Its predeclared transition required six completed decisions without a scored error.
The second stage allowed three fresh groups after that condition passed. No further search or retries were permitted.
The limit was nine requests per provider and 60 seconds per request, with no purchases or top-ups.
Native charges and a combined monetary ceiling remained unknown.

The native line remained gpt-6-astra at xhigh effort under Codex CLI 0.154.0.
The recipe froze before fresh-case authorship. Labels stayed outside both providers' input.
Each provider received the same bounded state and candidate descriptions. Native execution restrictions remained outside the target-task text.
Sources: [recipe](skill-policy-v3-20260920/recipe.json), [manifest](skill-policy-v3-20260920/manifest.json), and [input changes](skill-policy-v3-20260920/input-changes.json).

The recipe SHA-256 is `6204178a466f4666e85390efed91321ca25d654127cbb1db53b66ac54638f43e`.
The development cases SHA-256 is `25508bf3abe441e6bd96d09124145daddbe70efe499f3e651422a374f918635a`.
The fresh cases SHA-256 is `fae6fd015d47959e4cdf382352094a8e75c3ad49e95309ce3c0ba467c6539410`.

### Independent cases and label review

A bounded Sol/high consultation authored three source-anchored groups without seeing prior model outputs or the research report.
The groups covered skill-index specification, consumers output implementation, and release-process lookup.
The coordinator verified the consequential source facts before inference. Public GitHub bytes matched all 35 source files used by the combined trial.
Sources: [fresh cases](skill-policy-v3-20260920/fresh-cases.json), [freeze and adjudications](skill-policy-v3-20260920/fresh-manifest.json), and [public-source checks](skill-policy-v3-20260920/public-source-evidence.json).

The coordinator added the required specification fork and protected the known kit-authoring skills before inference.
The CLI label for specification remained disputed because the broad loading trigger and the command's AXI exemption did not settle its applicability.
The TDD label in that case also remained disputed. Neither disputed label contributes to binary error counts.
These agent-authored, source-checked labels are not independent human ground truth.

### Complete selection outcomes

| Partition and case | Required additions | Selected additions | Route | Scored result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Development: cache lookup | Empty | Empty | Jev | Pass |
| Development: roadmap specification | delegate, domain, seams, tickets | delegate, domain, seams, tickets | Fallback | Pass |
| Development: assessment lookup | Empty | Empty | Fallback | Pass |
| Development: gate-wrapper action | comments, gate; CLI protected | comments, gate | Fallback | Pass |
| Development: handoff terminology | Empty; domain protected | Empty | Fallback | Pass |
| Development: coverage review | seams | seams | Jev | Pass |
| Fresh: skill-index specification | delegate, domain, seams, spec, tickets | delegate, domain, seams, spec, tickets | Fallback | Pass |
| Fresh: consumers implementation | CLI, comments, tickets | CLI, comments | Fallback | Missing tickets |
| Fresh: release-process lookup | Empty | Empty | Fallback | Pass |

The table shortens `craft-*` IDs for readability. Section 19 preserves every full ID, probability, native explanation, and exact input link.
All nine decisions completed and preserved their protected sets. No clear wrong addition or abstention occurred.
Source: [scored results](skill-policy-v3-20260920/summary.json).

### What failed, and what remains uncertain

Jev assigned required craft-delegate probabilities of 0.12 in the exposed specification case and 0.09 in the fresh specification case.
Both were accepted negatives under the frozen band. Other uncertain candidates invoked fallback, which recovered those additions.
Jev assigned required craft-tickets 0.16 in the fresh consumers case. Native fallback also omitted it.
These observations again show that uncertainty elsewhere can hide an accepted-negative error without making that error safe.

The consumers label follows Bench's light-path requirement to author one ticket before implementation.
The supplied task said “one-ticket” update but did not explicitly request ticket authoring.
Its project facts also omitted that light-path rule. The native explanation said the supplied evidence established no further trigger.
This evidence gap limits attribution of the frozen scored miss. The result and label remain unchanged after inference.
Sources: `.bench/BENCH.md:137-140`, [frozen input](skill-policy-v3-20260920/fresh-consumers-dir-files-request.json), and [complete output](skill-policy-v3-20260920/fresh-consumers-dir-files-result.json).

The development gate case changed both task framing and the protected set. Its improved score cannot establish which change caused the outcome.
V3 used one observation per case, without a matched new control or repeated trials.
The fresh cases remain controlled prompts anchored to real source, not naturally occurring sessions or complete tasks.

### Time, usage, and cost

| Evidence partition | Jev input/output tokens | Native input/output tokens | Jev seconds | Native seconds | Routed policy seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Six exposed development cases | 31,093 / 1,653 | 114,146 / 1,963 | 2.500 | 101.779 | 73.381 |
| Three fresh controlled cases | 14,978 / 787 | 56,552 / 814 | 1.248 | 47.396 | 48.647 |
| All nine cases | 46,071 / 2,440 | 170,698 / 2,777 | 3.748 | 149.175 | 122.028 |

These are sums of measured monotonic durations. Native totals include independent reference calls on the two direct-Jev cases.
The routed policy excludes those two reference calls. Its seven fallback calls consumed 132,256 native input tokens and 2,299 output tokens.
All fresh cases used fallback, so Jev added measured request overhead there without avoiding a native call.

The published Jev input rate estimates $0.001934982 for V3. Actual charges remain unknown; this estimate excludes native costs.
Five request clocks differed between UTC elapsed time and monotonic duration by more than 0.01 seconds.
The [clock audit](skill-policy-v3-20260920/clock-audit.json) preserves both observations. Their discrepancy remains unexplained.

Fresh native selector processes remain comparison observations, not a measured existing-workflow baseline.
Bench's current reference tells agents to find relevant guidance through its skill index.
The inspected catalog owner generates and checks that index. It does not establish the marginal cost of an agent's inline selection.
Sources: `.bench/BENCH-reference.md:74-78` and `internal/skillsindex/skillsindex.go:1-9`.

### Validation and next evidence

Eighteen assessment inputs preserve separate provider usage and diagnostic outcomes. Seven native calls also served as the policy fallback.
Development records are exposed; fresh records carry the controlled holdout flag. This flag does not establish natural-task validity or default-change eligibility.
The existing Plan-schema limits remain. The [import registry](skill-policy-v3-20260920/assessment-imports.json) records each stored observation.

Nine local validator fixtures passed. They checked numeric boundaries, malformed answer rejection, candidate membership, duplicates, and valid empty selection.
These are parser-level checks. They did not test complete timeout, HTTP-failure, malformed-response, or failed-fallback execution routes.
Sources: [fixtures](skill-policy-v3-20260920/validator-fixtures.json) and [request ledger](skill-policy-v3-20260920/request-ledger.jsonl).

Before another candidate trial, make the required-skill evidence complete and measure the existing workflow on representative complete tasks.
Include evidence collection, requirement derivation, retained agent work, failures, and final task quality in that comparison.
Do not infer savings from avoiding an additional process that the existing workflow does not require.
Do not tune against these fresh results and continue calling them untouched evaluation.

Ticket #9 remains open for the missing evidence and live reviewer acceptance. Ticket #14 remains blocked, and compaction remains conditional.
The disposable provider runners are removed after their input and result copies are verified.
No closed endpoint, authority, fallback, scope, or roadmap decision changes.
